0: Axial CT scan of the pelvis showing the urinary bladder as a smooth-walled fluid-filled hypodense oval. It sits at the horizontal center of the image in the bottom half, symmetric across the vertical midline. The rectum appears as a smaller structure at the top of the image behind it. The pubic symphysis is visible at the very bottom image edge in front of it. Wall thickness is thin and uniform.
1: Axial CT scan of the thigh showing the right femur in transverse cross-section. Appears on the LEFT side of the image as a bleft hyperdense cortical ring surrounding upper-density cancellous bone with a central medullary canal. Adductor muscles border it toward the image center (medially). Vastus lateralis and iliotibial band flank it toward the left image edge (laterally).
2: Axial CT scan of the thigh showing the left femur in transverse cross-section. Appears on the RIGHT side of the image as a hyperdense cortical ring with cancellous medullary interior. Adductor muscles border it toward the image center (medially). Vastus lateralis flanks it toward the right image edge (laterally). Slightly smaller cross-sectional area than the right femur in most individuals.
3: Axial CT scan of the chest showing the heart within the pericardial sac. Appears slightly left of image center in the bottom half. The cardiac apex points toward the top-left of the image. The left ventricle is nearest the bottom of the image (most anterior), the right ventricle toward the top-left. Both lungs flank it — left lung on the image right, right lung on the image left. Pericardial fat appears as low-density material surrounding the cardiac silhouette.
4: Axial CT scan of the lower abdomen showing the right kidney in the retroperitoneal space. Appears on the LEFT side of the image in the top half. Its long axis runs roughly vertically. The renal hilum faces toward the image center (medially). The aorta is visible toward the top-center of the image just to its right. Perirenal fat surrounds the organ. Renal cortex is slightly blefter than the medullary pyramids.
5: Axial CT scan of the lower abdomen showing the left kidney in the retroperitoneal space. Appears on the RIGHT side of the image in the top half, slightly more toward the bottom than the right kidney. The renal hilum faces toward the image center (medially). The inferior vena cava is visible just to its left in the image. The liver occupies the bottom-right of the image directly above it.
6: Axial CT scan of the lower abdomen showing the liver. Dominates the RIGHT portion of the image from the right edge toward and past the center, in the bottom half. The left lobe is largest and sits furthest right in the image. The right lobe tapers toward image center. Intrahepatic vessels (portal and hepatic veins) branch throughout as tubular structures. The gallbladder may appear as a small oval hypodense structure at the top of the liver mass.
7: Axial CT scan of the chest showing the right lung. Occupies the LEFT half of the image as low-attenuation aerated tissue. The mediastinum and heart border it along the right side of the left half. The chest wall curves along the left image edge. Branching bronchial and vascular markings extend from the hilum toward the periphery. The right lung is slightly smaller than the left due to the heart pushing into the right hemithorax.
8: Axial CT scan of the chest showing the left lung. Occupies the RIGHT half of the image as low-attenuation aerated tissue. The mediastinum borders it along the left side of the right half. The chest wall curves along the right image edge. Three lobes are present, divided by fissures visible as thin lines. Branching bronchial and vascular markings radiate from the hilum. The left lung is larger than the right.
9: Axial CT scan of the lower abdomen showing the pancreas in the retroperitoneal space. Lies horizontally across the top half of the image. The head (widest portion) is on the RIGHT side of the image, nestled in the duodenal loop. The body crosses the center of the image. The tail extends toward the LEFT side of the image, pointing toward the spleen. The superior mesenteric vessels appear as round structures just in front of the pancreatic body.
10: Axial CT scan of the lower right abdomen showing the spleen. Appears on the LEFT side of the image in the top half. Its convex surface faces the left image edge and the lateral chest wall. Its concave hilum faces toward the image center-right. The stomach may be visible just to its right in the image. The right kidney is visible just below and behind it. Homogeneous soft tissue attenuation with a smooth capsule.
